title: Fix the Sorted-List Merge
statement: Read n, then n sorted integers (list A), then m, then m sorted integers (list B). The program below is supposed to merge A and B into a single sorted list using the classic two-pointer merge step, and print the result space-separated. It has 3 bugs. Fix them so it passes all test cases.
starter_code:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
m = int(input())
b = list(map(int, input().split()))

i, j = 0, 0
merged = []
while i < n and j < m:
    if a[i] >= b[j]:
        merged.append(a[i])
        i += 1
    else:
        merged.append(b[j])
        i += 1
merged.extend(a[i+1:])
merged.extend(b[j:])
print(' '.join(map(str, merged)))
hints: Walk through a small example by hand: which element should be picked first when a[i] and b[j] are equal, and which pointer should move each time?
Whichever list you didn't just take an element from is still at its original position - check every increment goes with the right pointer
Once the loop ends, the leftover slice of each list should start exactly at its current pointer, not one past it
